Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "hey can you help me put together a message for the library circulation desk about borrowing a scanner. it needs to be for Mina, not Quentin, so make the person the loan is for really clear. Mina is hoping to borrow one of the portable document scanners from the downtown branch for the weekend, starting friday afternoon and bringing it back monday morning. she wants to scan some family papers at home, not use a computer or scanning station at the library. ask whether a portable scanner is available for those dates and what the checkout and return process would be. if there’s a loan period or any equipment instructions she should know about, ask them to share that too. keep the message friendly and straightforward, and don’t make it sound like the scanner has already been reserved or that the library has confirmed anything. please make it a short email with a subject line. don’t write a reply from the library; just give me the prompt/request in a clear form so it can be used to draft the email.", "output": "Draft a short, friendly email to the library circulation desk, including a subject line, asking about a scanner loan for Mina, not Quentin. Mina hopes to borrow a portable document scanner from the downtown branch for the weekend, picking it up Friday afternoon and returning it Monday morning. She plans to scan family papers at home, rather than use a computer or scanning station at the library. Ask whether a portable scanner is available for those dates and what the checkout and return process would be. Also ask whether there is a loan period or any equipment guidance Mina should know about. Do not imply that the scanner has been reserved or that the library has confirmed its availability. Provide only the prompt for drafting the email, not a reply from the library."}]
